title: Global meromorphic continuation of Lie-derivative resolvents for smooth Axiom A flows with strong transversality on closed manifolds
source_title: A Morse complex for Axiom A flows
author: Antoine Meddane
difficulty_reason: The cited anisotropic spectral theorem does not provide a global escape function for a non-Anosov Axiom A flow with several basic sets and heteroclinic connections. The author constructs new compatible filtrations and cotangent-cone controls, then proves compactness of the global conormal distributions by following an increasing chain of basic sets. These results supply the complete global energy and escape construction needed to apply the precise published vector-bundle resolvent theorem on arbitrarily large half-planes.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Theorem1: smooth Axiom A vector field V on a smooth closed compact manifold M of dimension n>=1, satisfying the strong transversality assumptions11; for every degree0<=k<=n, the resolvent (Lie_V^(k)+z)^-1 from smooth complex k-forms to distributional complex k-forms is holomorphic on a sufficiently far right half-plane and extends meromorphically to all C. Full authored new energy/filtration31–36, cotangent cone control37–46, conormal compactness47–50, invariant neighborhoods51–53, and global escape construction54–58 read. Appendix generalized lambda lemma and Smale-order closure59–71 read. Spectral deduction26–29 explicitly invokes published Faure–Sjoestrand reference30 Theorems1.4/1.5 using only the escape properties identified in footnote9, with vector-bundle extension reference24 and variable-order elliptic calculus reference29 Lemma12; these are traced named background, not omitted new Axiom A core. Stable-manifold and Bowen product-structure references21/35 are likewise identified. No semisimplicity of zero resonance, ordinary invariant-form replacement, or separate cohomology-complex claim is counted. Original2025volume12 DOI10.5802/jep.299 and pinned acquisition date retained.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The author constructs global conormal attractor-repeller geometry, proves compactness and Smale ordering with a generalized lambda lemma, and assembles a microlocal escape function to obtain global resonance theory. This hyperbolic microlocal analysis exceeds ordinary qualifying examinations.
